Field: Physics / 02/PHYS-04 Fisica teorica della materia, modelli, metodi matematici e applicazioni

Extreme Learning Machines (ELMs) are feed-forward neural networks with a single hidden layer and random couplings, trained via linear regression, saving time and resources. Their quantum counterparts (QELMs) use a quantum reservoir to build complex representations of classical data, with inexpensive, noise-robust performance. The Quantum Theory Group at UNIPA has demonstrated the advantages of QELMs for validating and certifying quantum systems without tomographic reconstruction. The main purpose of the research project is to understand complexity in the context of the many-body problem, with particular reference to quantum simulators. Computational methods drawn from statistical mechanics, such as Monte Carlo methods and tensor networks, will be developed and employed.
